title: Distributed Semantics for Distributed Quantum Computing
summary: We present a quantum process calculus that can split the system state along process boundaries and follow the evolution of each process in isolation, without losing information about the joint state-a property we call spatial compositionality. Compositionality is the key to reasoning about any complex system, yet quantum process calculi have struggled to provide its spatial kind, which would enable analyzing a system one process at a time. Many a quantum process calculi have been proposed, but they invariably rely on a global state representation based on state vectors or density matrices,…
